chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who catches the Imam while he is sitting and reciting the Tashahhud, and there is only one man behind him on his right. He said: 'He should not go ahead of the Imam, nor should he lag behind that man, but the one who enters with him should sit behind the Imam. When the Imam gives the Salam, that man stands and completes his prayer.'

key_terms.يُدْرِكُ الْإِمَامَ: catches the Imam (joins prayer during Imam's action)

ai.seo_question: What should a latecomer do if they join the prayer when the Imam is sitting and there is only one person behind him?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical logistics of joining a late prayer (Qada) when the Imam is in the final sitting position, prioritizing the latecomer's placement behind the Imam to maintain congregational unity. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the structural integrity of the prayer even in constrained spaces, ensuring the latecomer completes their missed rak'ahs in proper sequence after the Imam's Salam.
